text: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish, and on which no yoke has ever been laid.
Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he shall take it outside the camp, and it shall be slaughtered in his presence.

versions.text: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and it shall be led outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וְהוֹצִיא is active with Eleazar as subject ("he shall bring it out"). The fully passive rendering obscures the priest's role and blurs the shift to the following impersonal verb ("it shall be slaughtered").

versions.text: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring it outside the camp, and it shall be slaughtered in his presence.
versions.explanation: "Bring" normally implies motion toward the speaker, which works against the sense of הוֹצִיא ("lead/take out"). "Take it outside the camp" is clearer when read aloud while keeping Eleazar as the active subject, as the earlier revision intended.

text: Then Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
The heifer shall be burned in his sight—its hide, its flesh, and its blood, along with its dung.
The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn, and throw them into the fire consuming the heifer.
Then the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, but he remains unclean until evening.
The one who burns the heifer shall also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he remains unclean until evening.

A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the community of the Israelites, to make the water of purification; it is a purification offering.

versions.text: A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They shall be kept by the congregation of Israel for the water of purification; it is a purification offering.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says the ashes are to be kept "for the congregation of the Israelites" as a charge (לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת), not kept "by" them; and the ashes are used to prepare the water of purification, which the added "to make" clarifies for a listener.

versions.text: They shall be kept in safekeeping for the community of the Israelites, to make the water of purification; it is a purification offering.
versions.explanation: The entire first half of the verse has been lost: וְאָסַף אִישׁ טָהוֹר אֵת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה וְהִנִּיחַ מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה בְּמָקוֹם טָהוֹר ("A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them outside the camp in a clean place"). Without it the pronoun "They" has no antecedent and the instruction about who gathers the ashes and where they are stored is missing, which also breaks the link to verse 10 ("the one who gathers the ashes"). The intentional changes from the earlier revision ("for the community of the Israelites" and the clarifying "to make") are retained; the redundant "in safekeeping" is trimmed since "kept" already carries לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת.

text: The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This shall be a lasting statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.
Whoever touches the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days.

He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a corpse, the body of a person who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the LORD's tabernacle. That person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him, he remains unclean; his uncleanness is still on him.
This is the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in it shall be unclean for seven days,
and every open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
Anyone out in the open who touches someone killed by the sword, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person they shall take some of the ashes from the burned purification offering, and fresh running water shall be poured over them in a jar.

versions.text: For the unclean person they shall take some of the ashes from the burned purification offering, and fresh water shall be poured over them in a vessel.
versions.explanation: מַיִם חַיִּים means literally "living water," that is, flowing or spring water rather than merely fresh water; "running" makes this clear. "Jar" also reads more naturally aloud than the abstract "vessel."

text: Then a man who is clean shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the vessels, and everyone who was there, as well as anyone who touched a bone, or one who was killed, or a dead body, or a grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean one on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall purify him. Then he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and by evening he will be clean.

But anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself shall be cut off from the assembly, for he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
This shall be a lasting statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening.
Whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it shall be unclean until evening.
